label: Higher when S1 is reached at D2, after reaching S2 at GO, and after no reward at D1.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * ((state == S1) * 1 - (state == S2)) ;; (phase == GO) * ((prev_state == S2) * 1 - (prev_state == S1)) ;; (phase == D2) * ((prev_reward == 1) * 1 - (prev_reward == 0))
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * prev_reward
explanation: Raw reset gate r34, which sits on top of a strong timing profile (GO high, D2 middle, D1 low). Beyond timing, the main driver is the state reached, shown at D2: S1 raises it by about 0.14 and S2 lowers it. At GO it is higher when the previous trial reached S2 (about +0.1; this matches the GO belief deciles, higher when S2 looks good). At D1 it is slightly higher after an unrewarded trial. The free fit adds: a lower value at D2 for the a2 choice given the state, a D2 boost when S1 was reached after a reward on the previous trial, and small graded belief_lo terms. No future variables are used. The full-fit dev R2 beyond timing is 0.79; the short form scores 0.64 on dev.

issues: The recorded short form uses one-sided indicators such as (phase==D2)*(state==S1). The fit has no phase-specific offset for these terms, so each term also has to shift its whole phase's mean. Misses on the recorded form show a phase-level bias: mean error D1 +0.024, D2 -0.025. Using signed versions of the same two main terms instead, e.g. (phase==D2)*((state==S1)*1-(state==S2)), raises test R2 beyond timing from 0.563 to 0.792 with only two terms. That is already above the free fit's 0.78.

Part of the D1 term's contribution (prev_reward==0) is an offset correction. It adds 0.075 to the one-sided form (0.563 -> 0.638), but only 0.010 once the first two terms are signed (0.792 -> 0.802). Alone it scores 0.008. The claim that D1 is higher after no reward is a weak effect and does not deserve a place in the label.

The recorded form's third term only works as a fitted correction, which shows it was fitting noise rather than describing the gate. Other examples: (phase==D2)*(prev_reward==0) scores 0.673 but its complement (phase==D2)*(prev_reward==1) scores 0.574, which should not happen if the term were a real effect.

A better third term, signed, is at D2: the gate is lower after an unrewarded previous trial (weight -0.024 on the +/-1 coding). Test R2 0.825. GO*belief_lo as the third term does almost as well (0.825). D2 action (0.801) and D2 common (0.793) add little.

Misses on the improved form leave no phase bias (D1 +0.002, D2 -0.002). The remaining errors are small (about 0.04 or less) and are at GO by previous choice: GO after a2 is higher than predicted, after a1 lower. This matches the free fit's GO*(prev_action==2) term.
The core claims hold: at D2, S1 is higher than S2, and at GO the gate is higher when the previous trial reached S2. No future variables are used.
skeptic.revised_label: D2: higher for S1 than S2 reached, lower after no reward; GO: higher after S2 than S1
